run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T22:30:18Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy continuously records error spans: at the last evaluation (22:51:00) the error-span increase was 5.297 over 8 minutes, i.e. ≈0.0110 errors/s ≈ 1 error per 90 s, numerically the same magnitude as the alert's reported current value 0.0111. frontend-proxy's own Envoy access log shows what those errors are: HTTP 503 with response flag UC = upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, attributed by the proxy to upstream cluster "frontend", on GET /api/products/*, /api/recommendations, /api/data and /api/cart. 14 such 503 UC lines occur between 22:11:20 and 22:29:05, and they continue after a short error-free lull (5m error increase 0 at the 22:27–22:30 evaluation points, nonzero again from 22:31). A separate, larger burst occurs at 22:33:18–22:33:20, when frontend-proxy logged HTTP 500 for POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, coincident with the cart Deployment rollout (new ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d created 22:32:48, revision 1→2, identical images/env; old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 killed 22:32:51). Cart and checkout themselves report zero error spans throughout, including the burst. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the frontend Deployment terminating upstream connections: the frontend container runs with a 100m CPU limit and 34–41% CFS-throttled periods and its V8 old_space heap sits at 33–48 MB against a ~44–52 MB heap limit (hypothesis, no baseline before 22:15). flagd's cartFailure="on" fault flag remains an unverified candidate. All otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0 for cart, frontend and frontend-proxy.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's only series in this Prometheus are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, and its status_code label only takes STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so the alert can only be backed here by span error counts.

At the 22:51:00 evaluation, frontend-proxy span_name=ingress status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR had an increase of 5.297 over 8 minutes (≈0.0110 errors per second, ≈1 error per 90 s) while span_name="router frontend egress" error increase was 0 in the same window; its non-error (UNSET) volume was ~1160 spans each.

frontend-proxy's Envoy access log shows its 5xx responses carry the flag "UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" with upstream cluster "frontend" (e.g. GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP 503 at 22:31:05, GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z 503 at 22:34:05).

14 HTTP 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} lines occur in frontend-proxy's log between 22:11:20 and 22:29:05 (≈1 per 77 s) against routes /api/products/*, /api/recommendations, /api/data and /api/cart, all from client python-requests/2.32.5 — i.e. these errors pre-date the alert start of 22:30:18.

The frontend-proxy 5-minute error increase was 0 at the 22:27, 22:28, 22:29 and 22:30 evaluation points, 1.11 at 22:31, 2.22 at 22:33, then 233.75 at 22:35 and 211.11 at 22:36–22:38, returning to ~5.6 at 22:39 — a short error-free lull followed by resumed sporadic errors and then a large burst.

At 22:33:18–22:33:20 frontend-proxy logged HTTP 500 responses served via_upstream from frontend for POST /api/cart (multiple), GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, e.g. "POST /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 500 at 22:33:18.190731Z.

frontend's own error spans rose from 0 at 22:31:18 to 23.56 (GET), 71.71 (POST), 23.56 (POST /api/cart), 53.27 (GET... POST /api/cart), 18.44 (POST /api/checkout), 76.83 (executing api route /api/cart), 23.56 (grpc CartService/GetCart), 53.27 (grpc CartService/AddItem), 18.44 (grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and 7.17 (tcp.connect) per 21-minute window from 22:36:18 onward.

cart and checkout report zero error spans in every 5-minute window across the incident, including the 22:35–22:39 points that contain the frontend's cart/checkout client errors, so neither service emitted its own error-status spans.

The cart Deployment rolled out during the window: events show Deployment cart ScalingReplicaSet up cart-84889c965d 0→1 at 22:32:48 and down cart-755465879b 1→0 at 22:32:51, ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d SuccessfulCreate at 22:32:48, pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz Scheduled/Created/Started 22:32:48–22:32:50, and pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 Killing at 22:32:51; ReplicaSet creation timestamps are cart-755465879b 22:01:38Z and cart-84889c965d 22:32:48Z.

The cart ReplicaSets revision 1 (cart-755465879b) and revision 2 (cart-84889c965d) have identical container definitions: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, the same env (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, CART_PORT, VALKEY_ADDR, FLAGD_HOST, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) and the same init container wait-for-valkey-cart.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json currently sets cartFailure to defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail cart service") while every other flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is defaultVariant "off".

The frontend container has a CPU limit of 100m (request 50m, memory limit 200Mi) and frontend-proxy has a CPU limit of 30m; the frontend container's CFS-throttled period ratio was 0.34–0.41 across 22:15–22:47, and its V8 old_space heap was 33.1–48.2 MB against a heap limit of 43.8–52.5 MB.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready at query time; restart counts are 0 for frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt and cart-84889c965d-tkxdz (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh shows restartCount 1).

Other services' error spans in the same window are near zero: accounting, payment, cart and checkout show 0; ad shows 1.11 per 5 min at 22:17–22:20 and 22:26–22:29; fraud-detection 1.11 at 22:14–22:15 and 22:25–22:28; recommendation 1.11 sporadically.

The persistent ~1-per-90 s 503 UC errors originate in the frontend Deployment: its pods terminate the upstream connection before responding (/api/products/*, /api/recommendations, /api/data, /api/cart), plausibly because the frontend container is CPU-throttled ~34–41% of CFS periods under a 100m limit and its V8 old_space heap runs 33–48 MB against a ~44–52 MB heap limit; the frontend's own error spans are 0 outside the 22:33 burst, consistent with it dropping connections before producing spans.

The 22:33:18–22:33:20 burst of frontend HTTP 500s on cart/checkout routes was caused by the cart Deployment revision 1→2 rollout at 22:32:48: with a single cart replica being replaced, callers of CartService (and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, which depends on cart) got failures, which the frontend surfaced as 500s; cart itself recorded no error spans for those requests.

flagd's cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") is a candidate fault-injection contributor to the cart-related failures, since it matches the observed failure path (frontend's grpc CartService/GetCart and AddItem error spans); however no sustained cart errors or gRPC failures are visible, so its runtime effect could not be confirmed and flagd's containers produced no readable logs.

The cart Deployment rollout does not explain the alert's start: the alert is stated to fire from 22:30:18, while the rollout events are timestamped 22:32:48–22:32:51 and 503 UC upstream-reset errors were already being logged from 22:11:20 to 22:29:05.

Pod-level damage is ruled out for the workloads involved: no Evicted, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling or Unhealthy events appear for otel-demo pods in the window, and cart, frontend and frontend-proxy containers show restartCount 0 with the Expected Created/Started/Pulled pod events.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule (it is not present in this Prometheus's rule set) to confirm its expression, window and the meaning of the threshold "above 0", since a threshold of 0 on a signal that carries sporadic upstream resets keeps the alert firing indefinitely.

Review the frontend Deployment's 100m CPU limit (and frontend-proxy's 30m) against observed throttling of 34–41%, and check the Next.js/Node keep-alive and GC behaviour, to determine whether the upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} 503s are resource-driven or a keep-alive reuse race.

Confirm who/what applied cart Deployment revision 2 at 22:32:48 (identical pod template in images/env) and check whether the cart rollout should use a surge/maxUnavailable setting that keeps a ready endpoint for this single-replica service, since the frontend returned 500s during the replacement.

gaps: The alerting rule for RequestErrorRate is not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for the whole rule set, so the expression, evaluation window and threshold behind the reported 0.0111 cannot be verified; the match with the observed ≈0.0110 errors/s is numeric correspondence only.

At exactly 22:30:18 the traces-based 5m error increase for frontend-proxy evaluated to 0, which is in tension with the reported alert start; the alert's own data source and evaluation timing remain unknown.

Jaeger returned no traces at all for the queried windows (traces_search for frontend and frontend-proxy over 22:20–22:51 and frontend over 22:30–22:36, and traces_search_by_tags error=true), despite listing 18 services; span-level status codes, gRPC status values and error messages for the failed cart/checkout calls are therefore unknown.
The frontend container produced no readable log output (0 bytes) for 21:30–22:51 and 22:25–22:40, so the frontend's own reason for terminating connections and for the HTTP 500s is unknown.
frontend-proxy logs older than 22:11:20 were not readable (4 MiB read limit reached while reading newest-first), so whether the 503 UC pattern existed before 22:11 is unknown.

flagd containers (init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) produced 0 bytes of logs, and change history is not integrated, so when and how cartFailure was set to "on" and whether flagd's runtime state matches the ConfigMap could not be verified.

No baseline exists before ~22:15:18 for the traces/container/V8 series (they start then), so it cannot be determined whether the frontend's ~34–41% CPU throttling and 33–48 MB old_space heap usage changed at the alert onset or are long-standing.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh shows restartCount 1 with container Created/Started events at 22:03:25 and 22:38:19 and 1.11 error spans per 5 min at times; the cause of that restart and whether it is related to this alert were not established, and its logs were not read.
Whether the Envoy 503 UC responses are genuine request failures or an idle keep-alive reuse race between frontend-proxy and the frontend could not be determined from available data.
next_steps: Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its label/threshold configuration from the Alertmanager/Prometheus that actually evaluates it.
Read the frontend pod's application logs at the source (if not written to stdout) and enable/inspect Node.js logs for requests terminating with 500 or aborted sockets around 22:11–22:51.
Compare Envoy upstream idle-timeout and the frontend's HTTP keep-alive timeout to test the connection-reuse-race hypothesis.
Verify flagd's runtime flag state (cartFailure) with the flagd UI or ResolveBoolean calls, and decide whether the cartFailure fault was intended.
Review cart Deployment rollout strategy and revisions (who applied revision 2 at 22:32:48) to avoid an endpoint gap for the single-replica cart service.
